decision.scopeOfAccept: ACCEPT of g18-input-corpus.v1 as a DESIGN-CONTRACT-CANDIDATE at 0 blockers, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no express reservation. The artifact remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, and carries DO-NOT-SEAL on its own terms. DR-107 is not SATISFIED, OBL-G18-FX-AUTHORING and OBL-ENCODING-RESERVED remain leftover-design on their owning joins, no fixture bytes are authored, no journal or adjacent structure is invented, no DR-G* row is added, and required-now remains 26.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: The journal prohibition is the one that needs reading rather than counting, and it would defeat a mechanical sweep outright. The word appears thirteen times — but the live G18 v2 corpus class is itself named 'crash at every journal write/fsync/rename/pointer and migration prepare/commit/abort/no-return transition', so the word is unavoidable at its three carriers and every other occurrence is a negation. The decisive test is structural: no record layout, field, ordering rule, fsync discipline, pointer encoding, rename protocol, lock grammar, lease API, solver, or filesystem path is described, and the complete bare-integer set is 1 and 26, so no offset, sequence number or generation counter exists either. The three named members are == equal to live G18 v2 at three carriers, each initial state asserts exactly its own member, and the live DR-G18 register cell independently carries all three in the same order. Cardinality matters here: G18 v2's namedCorpusNote explicitly names five things that are NOT live classes and must not be invented — concurrent analyze, generation activation under a live lease as a fourth class, two cache writers, self-update rollback, and purge — and all five are absent, with 'purge' occurring zero times. All three initialStates carry fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED with no digest, path or file name anywhere inside them. Both cited joins were re-measured at source rather than accepted: g18-leftover-join.v1 is DR-G18 / OPEN with OBL-G18-FX-AUTHORING true, and lifecycle-leftover-join.v2 is DR-107 / PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW with OBL-G18-FX-AUTHORING and OBL-ENCODING-RESERVED true — and both tokens are confirmed against their own live register cells. Worth noting that the subject carries no file08StatusToken of its own, which is right for an input corpus and removes the import-a-token failure mode that mattered on the leftover-joins reviewed alongside it. One structural difference I checked before treating it as anything: this artifact has no recordedInputs manifest and no remeasurementClause. No input corpus in the corpus has either, and its 21-key shape is identical to six sibling gate input corpora, so that is the class norm and not an omission; all nine cited files remain digest-pinned regardless. Twenty-three attacks run, twenty-three refuted, zero findings. Two things a coordinator may want: the artifact calls itself 'This catalog' three times despite being an input corpus, and in the namedCatalog role that referent is genuinely ambiguous — though both readings are true and the operative fields all say 'This artifact', so it is naming hygiene a successor could tidy. And G18 v2's leftoverNameNote sentence 'No leftover-join artifact for this gate exists' is now stale, since g18-leftover-join.v1 exists; the subject correctly cites the join rather than repeating the note, and the same staleness should be expected on the G08 and G19 chains. Disclosure: all four cited claude2 reviews are my own; every digest was recomputed from disk and every claim re-derived from live bytes.
